canonical_question: Is the 30 Å pressing depth comparable to the 21 Å coating thickness, and if so, does the indenter penetrate the coating into the matrix, potentially invalidating the coating-only wear analysis?

question_variants.question: Is the 30 Å pressing depth comparable to the 21 Å coating thickness, and if so, does the indenter penetrate the coating into the matrix, potentially invalidating the coating-only wear analysis?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The document confirms the pressing depth is 30 Å and the coating thickness is 21 Å, which mathematically implies penetration into the matrix (30 > 21). However, the text does not explicitly state that the indenter penetrates the coating or discuss the implications for coating-only wear analysis.

answers.answer: The model has a high entropy alloy coating of 21 Å thickness and the pressing depth was set to 30 Å. This indicates the indenter depth exceeds the coating thickness, implying interaction with the underlying matrix, though the text does not explicitly discuss the validity of the coating-only analysis.
answers.material: Cu matrix / FeNiCrCoCu high entropy alloy coating
answers.measurement_outcome: Indentation depth (30 Å) > Coating thickness (21 Å)
answers.boundary_limitation: No explicit discussion on how this penetration affects the analysis of coating-only wear.
evidence_spans: In the nanoindentation model, single crystal Cu was used as the matrix material and FeNiCrCoCu high entropy alloy was used as the coating material.
The same lattice types of both materials were set.
The model size of the Cu matrix was 100 Å × 100 Å × 55 Å, and the total number of atoms was 47,111.
